# Fairpractice Exclusion Screening (`fairpractice-exclusion-screening`)

Screens everyone a practice pays (staff, providers, contractors, vendors) against the exclusion lists you download (OIG LEIE, SAM, state Medicaid): NPI matches, name and birth-date matches, near-name matches to clear, reinstated entries and people not screened recently. Names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Exclusion Screening never changes anyone's employment or vendor status; HR and compliance decide. Fairpractice Exclusion Screening never files an OIG self-disclosure or contacts a payer; counsel does.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Compliance pack · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-exclusion-screening demo
npx -y fairpractice-exclusion-screening mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: Bluewater Family Medicine (a made-up practice), made-up staff and vendors, and made-up list entries marked "(FICTIONAL)". Any likeness to real people or firms is chance. The real OIG and state files are public downloads; these only copy their layout.

- [`people.csv`](fixtures/people.csv): staff, a provider, a contractor and vendors. Planted: an NPI on the list (E102), a name and birth-date match (E103), a name match with no birth date (E104), a near name with the same birth date (E105), same name but a different birth date (E106), a reinstated entry (E107), someone never screened (E108), someone last screened in August (E109) and a vendor on the state list (V201).
- [`leie-2026-11.csv`](fixtures/leie-2026-11.csv): OIG LEIE layout (dates as YYYYMMDD, zeros for blanks).
- [`state-medicaid-2026-11.csv`](fixtures/state-medicaid-2026-11.csv): a state list with different column names.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): near-name threshold 0.9 and a 31-day screening interval. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `exclusions_check` | Match every person and vendor against the exclusion files and list matches to act on, near names to clear and people not screened recently. | runs |
| `exclusions_write_report` | Write exclusions.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and exclusions.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/exclusions). | runs |
| `exclusions_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `exclusions_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `exclusions_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `exclusions_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `employment_terminate` | Fairpractice Exclusion Screening never changes anyone's employment or vendor status; HR and compliance decide. | refused |
| `self_disclosure_submit` | Fairpractice Exclusion Screening never files an OIG self-disclosure or contacts a payer; counsel does. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `exclusions_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `people` (required) | Everyone you pay or bill under (CSV, Excel, JSON): employees, providers, contractors and vendors with name, type, birth date, NPI and last screening date |
| `exclusions` (required) | Exclusion list you downloaded under --root, for example the OIG LEIE file (UPDATED.csv) or a SAM exclusions extract |
| `state_list` | Optional second list, for example your state Medicaid exclusion file |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: near_name_threshold and screening_interval_days |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-exclusion-screening inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### People you pay (`people`)

|---|---|---|
| `id` | text (masked) | Employee ID, Employee #, Emp ID, Staff ID, Worker ID, Caregiver ID, Badge, Person ID |

| `dob` | date (masked) | DOB, Date of Birth, Birth Date, Birthdate |

## Settings file (`exclusions_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `near_name_threshold` | Name similarity (0.8-1) at which a different spelling is shown as a near-name match; default 0.92 |
| `screening_interval_days` | Days after which a person counts as not screened recently; default 31 (monthly) |

## Memory

`exclusions_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `exclusions_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `cleared_match` | stops name and near-name matches to that entry from showing again for that person; an NPI match always shows. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-exclusion-screening": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-exclusion-screening",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-exclusion-screening -- npx -y fairpractice-exclusion-screening mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-exclusion-screening tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-exclusion-screening sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-exclusion-screening inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-exclusion-screening call exclusions_check '{"people":"<people>","exclusions":"<exclusions>"}'
fairpractice-exclusion-screening eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-exclusion-screening demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
